context: Daichi shows Sho the country autumn harvest.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: しょう、収穫、見にいこか。
lines.en: Hey Sho, come on — let's go see the harvest.
lines.style: Warm Kansai lilt. Generous, inviting tone with real affection underneath. Opens bright and keeps that brightness steady. The regional accent audible but not performed — lived-in warmth.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Small, genuine voice. Quiet certainty without hesitation. Soft steady warmth. Six years old and present in the moment — no performance, just real eagerness.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: お米、たっぷり、できたで。
lines.en: The rice came out perfect — there's so much of it.
lines.style: Kansai swing evident. Pride that isn't about himself but about what they grew together. Warm, almost tender. The 'de' at the end lands with gentle satisfaction, not boasting.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: We worked hard on that rice. Together.
lines.style: Soft, observant six-year-old voice. Slow, thoughtful delivery. Not just recounting — reflecting on what the work meant. Small but grounded. Genuine warmth without knowing he's being wise.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Autumn really is the best season, isn't it.
lines.style: Kansai warmth at full rest. Closes gently, almost philosophically. Tender without sentimentality. The 'ya na' lands like a satisfied sigh — time slowing down, presence settling in.
